subject: Standard-decimal arithmetic
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS 2026-08-31 (owner decision D-C; kb/Work PB167). r2a-r2d were already exact (binary square-and-multiply over Mul, which for exponents 1-4 performs the printed equivalent expressions digit-for-digit); PB145 had closed every measured wrong answer in the escapes. What remained was r2e's own constraint on the DEVELOPMENT: 'Operands used in the development of that value shall be in SDIDI form. All additions, subtractions, multiplications and divisions performed in the development of the result shall be performed in accordance with the corresponding rules in ISO/IEC 60559:2020' (cite.py --check verified) — and the development went through IEEE binary64 (Math.Pow on the non-integer arm, a Math.Log10 decomposition on the past-loop-bound escape), so it satisfied neither shall and the two arms were two DIFFERENT approximations of the same value. There is now ONE development, exp(operand-2 x ln operand-1), carried entirely on CobolDec Add/Sub/Mul/Div with argument reduction (ln: decimal exponent split + three exact square roots + the atanh series; exp: reduction by n*ln10 so the 10^n factor is an EXACT decimal exponent shift, then the Taylor series), plus one chosen special case: at |operand-2| = 1/2 the equivalent expression is FUNCTION SQRT(operand-1), whose standard-decimal value Sec.15.84.4 r2 fixes EXACTLY, so b ** 0.5 and SQRT(b) agree by construction (they DISAGREED before). CobolDecPowDevelopmentTests scans CobolDec.cs and fails if any binary64 transcendental returns. ⛔ TWO DEFECTS IN THAT FIRST LANDING WERE FOUND BY ITS OWN REVIEW FLEET AND FIXED IN THE SAME WAVE. (1) kb/Work PB267 - the past-loop-bound escape rebuilt the exponent from TryIntegerValue's magnitude, which CLAMPS at long.MaxValue, so every exponent past 2**63-1 was silently replaced by 9223372036854775807: (1 + 10**-33) ** 1.0E+20 answered a flat 1.0000000000000 where 1.0000000000001 is owed, and 0.9999999999999999 ** 1.0E+25 answered a silent 0 where the value is below the decimal128 range entirely. PowMagnitude now carries the exponent OPERAND (an SDIDI holds |operand-2| exactly, so there was never anything to reconstruct), and PowCore screens the ORDER of p x ln b before forming it so an out-of-range product takes Sec.8.8.1.5.2 r2's own two names rather than Mul's clamp, which would say OVERFLOW in both directions. ⚠ The disposition is NOT 'a clamped exponent with |base| != 1 is out of range': the closest SDIDI value to one is 1 +/- 10**-33 and (1 + 10**-33) ** 10**20 is in range, so that screen would be PB145's spurious size error again. (2) kb/Work PB269 - the logarithm's three-square-root argument reduction carries u = m^(1/8) at 34 SIGNIFICANT digits about 1, so Sub(u, One) cancelled away log10(1/delta) of them: measured 17.05 correct digits at the worst point of |m-1| <= 1/4 and EXACTLY ZERO at m = 1 + 10**-33, where the first root rounds back to 1 and ln m came out 0. LnReduced now takes the same atanh series over delta = m - 1 directly inside that band (Sub(m, One) is exact there), which measures 32.74 digits at the same worst point and uses no square root at all. WHAT IS CLAIMED, precisely: an r2e-conforming SDIDI development, NOT 34 correct digits
